drills.title: Special Ops Quick Calls
drills.description: Collapse, crowds, crashes, and weather. Make the call that keeps your crew alive and your patient breathing.

items.prompt: Arm trapped for 4 hours under rubble; USAR ready to lift.
items.why: Fluids before freedom; prepare for hyperkalemia.

items.prompt: Post-release ECG: peaked T waves, QRS widening.
items.why: Calcium stabilizes the cardiac membrane in hyperkalemia.

items.prompt: Crowd surge at a gate; people can't raise their arms.
options: Stop inflow, open exits, extract from edges
Use a PA to tell people to push
items.why: Relieve pressure first — compressive asphyxia kills fast.

items.prompt: Train derailed under overhead catenary lines.
Water flowing across the road, ~30 cm deep, patient on the other side.
options: Stop — request swift-water rescue / find another route
items.why: ~1 ft of moving water floats most cars. Turn around, don't drown.

items.prompt: Small aircraft crash with burning wreckage.
items.why: Upwind; burning composites release toxic fibers/gases.

items.prompt: Lone 5-year-old at the green area; an adult says 'that's my nephew'.
options: Verify identity per reunification protocol before release
items.why: Unaccompanied minors are released only to verified guardians.

items.prompt: Coach crash: you've found 41 people; manifest says 44.
items.why: Closed incident — account for everyone on the manifest.
Technology-dependent patients become critical when power fails.
